articles.headline: Yankees predicted to sign $85M former Silver Slugger finalist to revitalize World Series hopes
keyFacts: The New York Yankees were swept by the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League Division Series following a disappointing season.
Analyst Joe Najarian suggested the Yankees should sign former Silver Slugger finalist Seiya Suzuki to revitalize their offense.
Signing Suzuki would allow Aaron Judge to transition to a designated hitter role following his injury-plagued season.
body: The New York Yankees are heading into the offseason with several things to address. Both the regular season and postseason were major letdowns compared to the standards the organization has set.
The American League Division Series went about as poorly as it could have for New York. The Yankees were swept by their AL East rival, the Tampa Bay Rays, who would go on to play in the World Series.

“Tampa Bay is moving on to the American League Championship Series, to play the winner of the Cleveland Guardians-Chicago White Sox series, winning 4-3 to complete a sweep of the Yankees in the division series that affirmed the Rays' summerlong dominance of their division rival,” ESPN’s Buster Olney wrote.
It was an up-and-down season for the Yankees, as they were without Aaron Judge for much of it. Judge was also left off the ALDS roster because of his injury.

“Judge has made his position clear -- he wants to be part of everything that transpires this month. However, Judge’s strained right calf has not healed enough for him to claim a spot on the 26-man roster for the Yankees' showdown against the Rays in the American League Division Series,” MLB.com’s Bryan Hoch wrote.
With Judge coming off an injury, SI’s Joe Najarian believes the Yankees should sign Seiya Suzuki and allow Judge to take on a designated hitter role.

“The Yankees would need to make quite a few moves to make this work, though. Because Suzuki is a full-time right fielder, Aaron Judge would become the everyday DH while Spencer Jones and Cody Bellinger play center and left field, respectively. It would also mean getting rid of both trade deadline additions (Luis Garcia Jr. and Heliot Ramos) and Giancarlo Stanton. But after his injury-plagued season, Judge will inevitably be limited to DH duties in the future. And given how good Suzuki was in 2026, the Yankees' post-Judge outfield would be in very good shape if they sign the Japanese slugger,” Najarian wrote.

Suzuki could be a strong addition to New York's lineup, particularly given his raw power and the short porches at Yankee Stadium. With his power at the plate, he could help bolster the Yankees' offense while allowing Judge to spend more time at designated hitter.

Suzuki recently completed his $85 million contract with the Chicago Cubs. He has been a Silver Slugger finalist twice during his MLB career, making him an intriguing potential addition to New York's lineup. If the Yankees pursue him, he could provide another offensive weapon as the organization looks to get back into World Series contention.

articles.headline: 'I'm going in the right direction' - Phil Foden hungry for more goals after starring with treble in Manchester City's 5-1 win over AEK Athens
keyFacts: Phil Foden scored three goals and provided one assist to help Manchester City secure a 5-1 victory over AEK Athens in the Champions League.
Head coach Maresca gave European debuts to several young academy players as the team managed an ongoing injury crisis.
Manchester City will travel to face Aston Villa on Saturday for their next Premier League match.
body: Manchester City v AEK Athens - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 - Getty Images Sport English playmaker inspires Etihad rout

Foden is determined to keep building his goal tally after registering a treble and an assist during the Citizens' 150th Champions League fixture . Having been sent off in last month's Manchester derby before ending a scoring drought dating back to December at the weekend, he now boasts four goals in four days. Victory also provided the ideal response to last week's 4-2 home defeat against holders Paris Saint-Germain .
Tactical switch unlocks clinical display

Tactical switch unlocks clinical display The hosts opened the scoring when Elliot Anderson poked home his first goal for the club after fellow summer signing Enzo Fernandez clipped a free-kick against the crossbar, before Foden converted Rico Lewis' pass. Seven minutes after the restart, Stavros Pilios netted the first goal City had ever conceded against Greek opposition following four previous clean sheets against Aris and Olympiacos, only for Foden to tee up Rayan Cherki and add two further strikes .

Expressing his delight with the collective performance while naming his second strike into the top corner as his favourite in a post-match interview with the club's official website , Foden said: "I enjoyed that a lot. The lads were great again. We showed determination again, it wasn't pretty at times. We were giving sloppy passes away. But, we stuck at the game plan and we kept going and in the end we broke them down. Overall I'm delighted.

"[My favourite goal is] probably the second to be honest. The way it went in. I'm delighted to score goals now, I'm a forward so I have to keep scoring and helping the team. It'll only do good for my confidence."

Reflecting on his bid to recapture peak form following two indifferent seasons and his enjoyment of a central attacking role, he continued: "Slowly but surely [getting back to my best], still got a long way to go. I'm going in the right direction. Scoring along the way definitely helps.

"I've just got to keep working hard and try to be as best as I can for the manager and for the team. Especially when I changed into the false 9 role, I really enjoyed it a lot. In between the lines and in the pockets where I like to be and linking the play. I really enjoyed that role tonight."
Academy graduates earn European bows

With top scorer Erling Haaland left unused on the bench following a recent injury scare, head coach Maresca handed Champions League debuts to youngsters Floyd Samba, Allan, Ryan McAidoo, Vitor Reis and Kaden Braithwaite.

Meanwhile, Foden's treble took him to 23 goals in the competition proper, moving him clear of Steven Gerrard (21) and level with Frank Lampard among Englishmen behind Harry Kane (57), Wayne Rooney (30), Raheem Sterling (27) and Paul Scholes (24).

Detailing how he is helping to guide the club's emerging prospects amid an ongoing injury crisis, Foden added: "Just trying to help them as best as I can, along with the captains, like Ruben [Dias] and Erling. Trying to help the young ones.

"It shows the trust the manager has. We've got a lot of injuries at the moment and he's not scared to use the young lads. They've been playing really well so they deserved to play tonight. I'm really happy for them."
Domestic leaders face Villa test

Domestic leaders face Villa test Getting their European campaign back on track provides the ideal platform for City as they look to preserve their flawless start in the Premier League. Maresca's men will travel to face Aston Villa on Saturday for a 12:30 BST kick-off. With Haaland well rested and Foden firing on all cylinders, the visitors should be well equipped for a testing afternoon at Villa Park.

articles.headline: Bryce Underwood's Michigan future bleak after Kyle Whittingham's call before Indiana game
keyFacts: Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood was benched for Tommy Carr during the win against Penn State after struggling with completions and interceptions.
According to reports, freshman quarterback Tommy Carr will receive his first career start for the Wolverines against the Indiana Hoosiers.
Coach Kyle Whittingham stated that the quarterback change was made to spark the offense after a scoreless first half.
body: The Michigan Wolverines didn't waste any time regarding which quarterback will start Saturday when they host the Indiana Hoosiers on Big Noon Kickoff (noon ET, FOX) in Ann Arbor.
Although the Wolverines beat Penn State 21-18 last week, quarterback Bryce Underwood was benched after throwing two interceptions and completing only 5 of 11 pass attempts for 43 yards.

In a relief effort, Tommy Carr replaced Underwood. Although Carr, a freshman quarterback who had previously appeared in a 52-17 win against UTEP, threw only two passes, the limited sample size was enough for the Wolverines to make a change with a little over a month left in the regular season.

According to On3's Pete Nakos, Carr will get his first career start. It's unclear whether this move will remain permanent, but given coach Kyle Whittingham's previous uncertainty surrounding Underwood, it's apparent that the move was going to happen sooner rather than later.

"Well, he only had about 70 yards or thereabouts in the first half, and no points, and we just needed to get something done and create a spark, as we said," Whittingham said after the win when asked about Underwood.
The plan seemed to work, as the Wolverines took control in the second half to snap their two-game losing streak.

"He's always prepared. I walk by the quarterback room 12 times, 15 times a day," Whittingham said of Carr's dedication. "He's in there pretty much every second he doesn't have class, he's in there watching film. So, he's very prepared when his number was called. Like I said, he responded very well. Going forward, we'll take a good, hard look at the tape and see why things bogged down in the first half and why we were a little better in the second half, because there really wasn't a lot of scheme change."
During his Monday presser, Whittingham wasn't prepared to name Carr as the Week 8 quarterback.
Now that it's reportedly official, it raises more questions about where the Wolverines' season goes from here.

Regardless of who the quarterback is, however, ESPN's Kirk Herbstreit said Whittingham could be on thin ice when it comes to his job security should he be unable to fix the current struggles Michigan is facing.
"And I know by doing that, if it doesn't work out, you know, you probably get fired, Herbstreit said on the "Nonstop" podcast.
So, in a nutshell, transitioning to Carr may be a last-ditch effort to save the Wolverines' season.
The question remains, however: will it?
As Saturday approaches, we'll have our answer soon.

articles.headline: Why does Elon Musk want to merge Tesla and SpaceX?
keyFacts: Elon Musk said he is considering merging Tesla and SpaceX, with special committees formed to assess the potential deal.
Musk stated that bringing the companies together would combine their technology projects and support his mission to colonize Mars.
The proposed merger requires approval from half of Tesla's shareholders, which Musk described as a high hurdle.
body: - Published
Elon Musk has spent years building Tesla and SpaceX into a pair of trillion-dollar technology empires. Now, he is considering bringing them together.
Asked on Tuesday whether a merger would be a good idea, Musk was clear: "Yes."

The prospect is more than hypothetical. Musk said special committees have been formed to assess a potential deal, although he stressed that there is no guarantee a merger will happen and that nothing has been agreed.
With Tesla valued at roughly $1.5tn (Â£1.1bn) and SpaceX at $2tn (Â£1.5bn), a combination of the two companies would mark the largest merger ever.
Any deal would also need shareholder backing. But Musk said he saw "a lot to be gained" in bringing the businesses together.
How likely is the merger?
"In my opinion, 100%. It's just a question of when," says David Nicholson, the Chief Technology Advisor at The Futurum Group, a market research company.

The unveiling of the Tesla Roadster last week - a futuristic electric car powered by SpaceX rocket thrusters - served as a "symbolic embodiment" hinting at the two Musk companies merging, Nicholson said.
Musk, the CEO of both SpaceX and Tesla, said bringing the firms together would be beneficial given the work each does around chips, artificial intelligence (AI) and other technology projects.
Specifically, the deal would combine Tesla's cars, robots and self-driving technology with SpaceX's rockets, data centres, satellites and telecommunications operations.
The move could be a step towards Musk's mission to build a self-sustaining city on Mars - a vision that has invited sceptics but also plenty of backers.
Over the past year, Musk has moved to consolidate his businesses, with SpaceX acquiring xAI and X, formerly Twitter, before going public this year.

But the merger would ultimately be decided by shareholders, with half of Tesla's needed to back the deal, a threshold even Musk described as "quite a high hurdle". Musk, as CEO of both companies, cannot participate in shareholder discussions.
Even so, Musk, a key shareholder of Tesla, will likely get his way in the next few years, said investment analyst Dan Sheehan from Telos Wealth Advisors.
He believes shareholders will back the deal as the technology the companies develop complement each other, Sheehan said.
But the merger would mean that Tesla shareholders will likely hold a "smaller slice of a much larger and more complex business," he added.
"There's no real precedent for how a public company like Tesla gets priced in this," Sheehan said.
SpaceX shares rose 8% in after hours trading while shares of Tesla climbed by 1.5%.
What would it mean for customers?
Experts told the BBC that Tesla drivers are unlikely to see much drastic change in the near term, even if the two companies combine.
In fact, vehicles seem almost like "an afterthought", overshadowed by the potential to combine the Tesla and SpaceX's tech capabilities, Nicholson said.
Changes are already underway at Tesla. The carmaker said earlier this year that it would prioritise its best-selling Model Y and Model 3, shifting focus away from less popular models.
Tesla also started using a manufacturing plant in California to produce humanoid robots, known as Optimus.
Pairing Tesla's self-driving technology and robotics with SpaceX's AI and satellite network could result in more capable vehicles, Sheehan said.
"The question is how much priority cars get inside a company increasingly driven by AI infrastructure," he added.
The recent Roadster showcase suggests SpaceX technology could be pulled into future Tesla products, which could attract more customers, said Tu Le, the founder of advisory firm Sino Auto Insights.
The Cybertruck-maker faces intense competition from Chinese carmakers like BYD, which overtook Tesla as the world's biggest EV maker in January.
What does Musk get out of it?
The biggest winner is probably Musk - the world's richest man who also became the world's first trillionaire earlier this year.
The merger would give Musk greater voting control over the combined company than he currently has at Tesla, a factor the special committee assessing the deal would have to consider.
A single company makes it easier for Musk to run his AI strategy the way he wants, Sheehan said.
"The deal itself doesn't add to Musk's wealth, but it concentrates it further in one stock," he said.
However, the merger could attract scrutiny over Musk, already a polarising figure in the US, Nicholson said.
The move could also face more regulatory pressure if Democrats - many of whom have been critical of Musk - win more seats in the US midterm elections next month.
Shareholders have backed Musk's desires before. Last year, Tesla investors approved an unprecedented compensation package for Musk valued around $1tn.
"I honestly don't think Musk will be keeping track of what the merger will do for his wealth," Nicholson said.
The deal also brings Musk closer to what Nicholson says is "his mission in life": colonising Mars.

articles.headline: Italy approves sweeping security measures in response to protests
keyFacts: Italy approved deploying 500 troops to Milan and introduced harsher legal penalties following violent cost-of-living protests over the weekend.
Demonstrators protested soaring fuel prices, high rents, and low wages, with some youths clashing with police and looting shops in northern cities.
Under new measures taking effect immediately, individuals endangering public safety face up to five years in prison, and parents face damage liability.
body: Italy has approved the deployment of troops and tougher legal penalties in a bid to quell cost-of-living protests in the north of the country that occasionally turned violent over the weekend.

The Italian cabinet on Tuesday approved sending 500 troops to Milan, a new legal offence covering violent participation in a demonstration, tougher penalties for rioters and financial liability for parents whose children take part in vandalism and looting.
Italy’s Ministry of Defence said the military will help reinforce security at key sites, step up surveillance of sensitive locations and enhance monitoring.

Unrest swept northern Italian cities at the weekend, including the financial capital Milan, where groups of mainly young people looted shops, smashed windows and clashed with the police. The demonstrations were driven by anger over soaring fuel and energy prices, high rents, low wages and the state of public services.
Public safety

As part of the new legal measures, which take effect immediately, anyone who takes part in a group of at least five people and endangers public safety during protests faces up to five years in prison and a maximum fine of €20,000 ($22,460).
Penalties increase if faces are concealed or people are injured.
Authorities can order prompt compensation for any damage inflicted and, in the case of minors, hold their parents liable.

Police will be allowed to detain youths aged between 14 and 17, even if they have not committed a crime, provided there is evidence they pose a danger, extending powers that previously applied only to adults.
But the cabinet did not approve giving soldiers policing powers, as expected, after opposition from President Sergio Mattarella, Italian media reported.
“Destroying and stealing is not protest, it is crime, and the state’s response must be firm,” Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said in a social media post after the cabinet meeting.
Echoing protests
The disturbances in northern Italy echoed riots in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country’s most violent turmoil in years.

Meloni’s government is also facing mounting pressure from a separate wave of protests in southern Italy, where truck drivers angered by soaring diesel prices and the rising cost of living have staged roadblocks that are disrupting supply chains.
Protesters in both the north and the south say rising prices are pushing families into poverty, a concern for Meloni ahead of the 2027 national elections.

articles.headline: Trump speaks for nearly 2 hours at North Carolina midterm rally — says he’s ‘working like a dog’ to get Republicans elected
keyFacts: President Trump spoke for nearly two hours at a North Carolina rally, actively campaigning to help Republicans get elected.
GOP Senate candidate Michael Whatley joined Trump onstage while trailing Democratic opponent Roy Cooper by nearly 10 points in recent polling averages.
Trump stated he is scheduled to hold another North Carolina appearance and approximately 18 rallies before Election Day.
body: President Trump stood on stage for nearly two hours Tuesday at a midterm rally in North Carolina, where he touted the grueling schedule he’s keeping to get Republicans elected in November.
Trump noted his whirlwind tour aimed at helping the GOP maintain control of Congress differs from how he’s previously approached midterm elections — and emphasized that it’s hard work.
“I’m doing something different. I’m working like a dog,” he told rallygoers in Greenville.
“When I wasn’t running, I didn’t really campaign,” Trump explained. “I let other people campaign. I figured that’s it. What did I know?”
However, with Republican candidates trailing or locked in tight races in several red states, Trump outlined plans last month to hit 35 battleground districts before the midterms.
The president has made 17 campaign stops since the GOP’s two-day midterm convention in Dallas last month.
“I’ve done like 10 rallies in about eight days,” Trump said, revealing that he’s scheduled to make another appearance in North Carolina before Election Day.
“We have like 15 days [before Election Day], and I’m doing about 18 rallies,” he continued. “That’s work.”
The president held the podium for roughly onw hour and 52 minutes, making his appearance in Greenville one of the lengthiest of the cycle and in recent memory.
Trump invited GOP Senate hopeful Michael Whatley and several other down-ballot Republican candidates in the Tar Heel State up on stage to deliver brief remarks.

Whatley, who is running to replace retiring GOP Sen. Thom Tillis, trails his Democratic opponent, former Gov. Roy Cooper, by nearly 10 percentage points in the latest RealClearPolitics average of polls.
Trump won the state in the 2024 presidential election by about 3 percentage points.
The president also invited NASCAR legend Richard Petty up on stage to speak, who compared the upcoming elections to a “big race.”
“This is the best driver we’ve ever had,” Petty said of Trump. “So what we’ve got to do is, you all have got to pick out the best pit crew … and that’s what all this is about.
“Let’s get out and get the very best pit crew we can for the best driver.”

articles.headline: US envoy to meet Putin in Russia as Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now'
keyFacts: US special envoy Steve Witkoff met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo to discuss proposals to end the war.
Zelensky said intelligence sharing with the US on Russian missile attacks works now, following earlier accusations of withheld intelligence.
Witkoff is scheduled to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday, while Russian officials ruled out making political concessions.
body: - Published
US special envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss proposals on ending Russia's years-long conflict with Ukraine.
The talks come one day after Witkoff's meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo, which a US official described as "constructive".

Kyiv previously accused the US of withholding key intelligence - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by Washington. Zelensky said on Tuesday that intelligence sharing with the US on Russian missile attacks "works now".
Zelensky and his European allies said it was now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo when Witkoff meets Putin on Wednesday.
Finnish President Alexander Stubb, who also took part in the talks, said "genuine progress" was made on proposals to achieve peace but gave no details and warned that patience would be needed.
Witkoff was not present at the joint press conference after Tuesday's talks in the Norwegian capital. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, another key envoy, took part in the meeting via video link.
A US official later described the talks as "very productive and constructive", saying there was a "strong alignment at the working level" among the US, Ukraine and Europe on "the next steps".
The official confirmed that Witkoff is due to meet President Vladimir Putin in Russia tomorrow to discuss the proposals and that Kushner will again participate virtually.

Putin is yet to publicly comment on the latest developments, but Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov earlier said the Kremlin would listen to what Wiktoff would offer, while ruling out "any political concessions".

Relations between Ukraine and the US have soured in recent weeks to the extent that Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president, and most recently "for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine".

Ahead of next month's US midterm elections, Trump has also sought to blame Ukraine's attacks on Russian oil refineries for fuel prices which have been rising since the start of the US-led war on Iran.

Speaking after Zelensky's news conference in Oslo, Trump again told reporters at the White House he wanted Kyiv to "make a deal". He said Russia would like to "get it done" and it was "time for Ukraine to end this war".
Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

Russian drone attacks have continued this week. Ukrainian officials said at least 10 people were killed on Tuesday - four in Kyiv and the capital region, another four in the eastern Donetsk region, and two in the central city of Dnipro. Another attack overnight on Wednesday killed two more people near Kharkiv, the country's second-largest city.
Addressing the issue of US intelligence sharing after Tuesday's talks, Zelensky said he was "thankful that intelligence works now".

"Speaking about early warning, which is very important for our people, our children, adults, civilians because we can hear when ballistic[s] is coming - so we are thankful to American side, now it works, it's great," the Ukrainian president said.

He said he also hoped for a good result on SpaceX's Starlink satellite access as well, after Ukraine's military had reported in recent days speed restrictions on the US platform used by Kyiv to carry out drone strikes against Russia.
Before the Oslo talks, Zelensky said he had had a "constructive discussion" with Rubio about the need for US early warnings, missile interceptors and Starlink.
Last week, a bipartisan group of US senators called for an urgent investigation into speed restrictions to the Starlink network in Ukraine.
And Zelensky also restated that Ukraine was "ready for negotiations" to end the war.
"Of course, we are not losing this war, but we are losing people because Russia attacks," he said.
The Ukrainian leader added that "strong" security guarantees for Ukraine were also discussed in Oslo, as well as energy ceasefire proposals.
Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr StÃ¸re, who also took part in the talks, stressed that Europe "needs to be at the table" during any discussions about how to end the Russia-Ukraine war.

Unconfirmed reports earlier on Tuesday said the transfer of more US-made Patriot interceptor missiles - the only effective weapon in shooting down Russian ballistic missiles - had not yet been approved.

Rubio, who is currently on a visit to India, admitted to reporters that it may be true that Patriot interceptors had not yet arrived in Ukraine - but he stressed that nothing had been denied to Kyiv intentionally.
European leaders meanwhile have expressed concern about recent US statements from the US towards Russia.

On Monday, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz spoke of "mixed pictures and messages" on the war, adding that he was trying to convince the American government "in total that this is something we have to resolve jointly".

"It's really a big effort for our budgets, it's really a big thing for the European Union, but we are doing that and we are trying to keep on doing that until this terrible war ends," the German leader told Bloomberg TV.

Asked during an interview on Monday whether or not he saw Ukraine as a US ally, US Vice-President JD Vance said Kyiv was "certainly a partner in some ways, but we have some divergent interests from time to time, like for example... I think they should stop bombing Russian energy".

"We don't have a formal alliance as far as I know with Ukraine. They're not in Nato, I don't think they should be in Nato... we're gonna work together on some things, but also we're going to be opposite on some things too," he said.

articles.headline: Grading LeBron James' 76ers debut: The King gets sterling marks as Philly spoils Knicks' title celebration
keyFacts: LeBron James made his debut for the Philadelphia 76ers in a 106-100 victory over the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.
James contributed 14 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists in 34 minutes of play during his first game with the team.
NBA commissioner Adam Silver stated that James using a helicopter provided by Fanatics complies with league rules.
body: The biggest story of the offseason is now a regular-season reality. The new NBA campaign tipped off on Tuesday, and with it we got our first glimpse of LeBron James in a 76ers uniform.

It went about as well as James and his new team could have possibly hoped in their inaugural outing together. The Sixers beat the Knicks 106-100, spoiling ring and banner night for the defending champions in Madison Square Garden.

In 34 minutes, James supplied his usual all-around excellence by stuffing the stat sheet: 14 points, nine rebounds, seven assists and just one turnover. Here are our grades for James from his first game with Philly.
Overall impact: A

James recently said the luxury of his game is that he can "literally do everything." He's not lying. James doesn't need to be the primary scorer to influence the proceedings and help his team win. That was true against the Knicks. He got off to a slow scoring start before finishing with 14 points on 5 for 13 shooting. He missed all three of his 3-point attempts. That's not great efficiency. It didn't matter.

In 34 minutes, James had nine rebounds, seven assists and helped the Sixers' defense make life difficult on the Knicks, who shot just 37% from the floor and 33% from 3-point range. If those are the kinds of numbers and effort they can expect from the 41-year-old James going forward, Philly will happily take it.
Q: "1-0, LeBron. What are your takeaways from your debut with your new team?"
LEBRON: "I liked the way we played... Good win for us."@KingJames and the @sixers win their season-opener at MSG! pic.twitter.com/gQDWPAZOiP
— NBA (@NBA) October 21, 2026
Pregame pomp: A

Selling James as a Sixer isn't a very heavy lift. You've got a franchise that hasn't been out of the second round in 25 years, and then the greatest player of all time comes along to save the day. The narrative writes itself.

So do the hype videos. Put James in a sweatshirt with "Phila" across the front, have him do a little voice-over about being excited to play for something that's about more than just him, do some tracking shots of the city and the fans, and add a "throw the ball up" tagline. Boom. As they say in Hollywood, that's lunch.

Slam Magazine also did a classic cover shoot with James. Full marks for going with "allow me to reintroduce myself," a line from Jay-Z's "Public Service Announcement," a track from "The Black Album," which was released in 2003, the same year James was drafted.
Public service announcement: tell 'em Bron still doing it.
LeBron James kicks off Year 24 on the cover of SLAM 265.
👑 https://t.co/fJoMhpxS3A pic.twitter.com/f6W6tTOaua
— SLAM (@SLAMonline) October 19, 2026
The marketing machine has been in overdrive and won't be slowing down anytime soon.
Cleared for takeoff: A

Earlier on Tuesday, NBA commissioner Adam Silver was asked about the much-discussed matter of James flying in a helicopter provided by Fanatics as part of his endorsement deal with the company. Michael Rubin, a former Sixers minority owner and the CEO and founder of Fanatics, added some fuel to that particular conspiracy fire. And Pablo Torre, who won a Pulitzer for his reporting on the Clippers cap circumvention scandal, is looking into the matter. But to hear the commissioner tell it, he sees nothing untoward about the arrangement.

"In the case of LeBron and that helicopter, he has a deal with Fanatics. It's perfectly appropriate if part of his deal is they're gonna supply a helicopter to him," Silver said. "I mean, as long as it's just a deal between the Fanatics and LeBron and no team is involved, there's no rules issue there whatsoever."
That has to come as a relief to James, whose commute from New York to Philly would get a lot more hectic if he had to travel up and down the New Jersey Turnpike.
Gameday fit: B

Not exactly his most memorable outfit. Nothing flashy here, just all business with a dark, double-breasted suit, a crisp white shirt and no tie to go with sunglasses and a bag. Vintage from head to toe.
24th season introduction: C

This one is complicated. James plays for the Sixers. He was introduced for the first game of his record-extending 24th NBA season in New York. That will automatically earn you some boos from the local fans, and rightly so. But James has often talked about how much he loves playing at Madison Square Garden, and there was quite a bit of chatter this offseason about how he dreamed of one day becoming a Knick. All of which led to a bit of a mixed reaction from the crowd when the PA announcer called his name as the fifth starter for Philly. Knicks fans can be forgiven for being uncertain about how to act on this one (though they stepped up their game later with a new chant).
Handshake with Joel Embiid: A+
It's the first game and Embiid has already roped him into doing D-Generation X cosplay. No notes.
First Sixers chalk toss: A
Classic.
First assist: B

When asked during the preseason how he anticipated utilizing LeBron, head coach Nick Nurse pointed to James's playmaking and said he'd help initiate the offense. Makes sense. James is one of the best passers of all-time.

For his first assist in a Sixers jersey, James saw Jaylen Brown in the paint, found the right angle as he so often does, and made a quick entry pass for an easy bucket. Much like LeBron's gameday fit, it wasn't exactly flashy, but it worked.
First field goal: C

Among other things, James is the all-time leader in points and field goals made. This basket will…add to those numbers. Picking on Landry Shamet in the post probably isn't something that will make his career highlight reel, but James had to get his first basket somehow.
First dunk: B-

The business end of an alley oop off a pass from Brown. This is sort of graded on the LeBron curve. He's one of the most explosive dunkers ever, but he's also going to be 42 in December. As far as his all-time dunks go, this won't be that memorable, but it's still impressive how athletic the man remains.
Running the break: A

James has been one of the best players in the open floor for nearly a quarter century. It's a sight to behold. Last season, he finished second in the NBA in total fastbreak points -- behind only new teammate Tyrese Maxey. In the third quarter, Maxey found him on a hit ahead and James did what he does best: accelerating toward the basket and finishing in transition at full speed. Josh Hart briefly made a half-hearted attempt at stopping the ball before thinking better of it. Smart man.
Correcting misinformed Knicks fans: A+

If you're gonna trash-talk (arguably) the greatest player of all time, at least get the guy's bio right. As for LeBron, the surest way to win over Philly's collective heart is to yell at an overbearing Knicks fan on national TV.
Spoiling ring night at MSG: Unknown

articles.headline: Marvel Officially Made the Saddest Death in MCU History More Tragic With Just 1 Sentence
keyFacts: In the series VisionQuest, the artificial intelligence F.R.I.D.A.Y. reveals she ran a quintillion strategic calculations trying to save Tony Stark when he died.
The article explains that despite calculating a quintillion scenarios during Avengers: Endgame, F.R.I.D.A.Y. could not find a way to save Stark's life.
The Polygon article states this new detail highlights the emotional depth and grief of synthetic life forms like F.R.I.D.A.Y. after Stark's death.
body: In Avengers: Infinity War, when Dr. Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch) and a variety of other heroes are awaiting Thanos’ arrival on Titan, Strange uses the Time Stone to look into alternate futures to see the possible results of the impending conflict. Star Lord (Chris Pratt) asks Strange how many futures he looked into, and Strange replies, “14,000,605.” Then Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.) asks how many of those resulted in their victory. Strange, looking deep into Stark’s eyes, says, “One.”

That one scenario involved Strange giving up the Time Stone to Thanos, letting him snap away half of existence, and, ultimately, Iron Man sacrificing himself at the end of Avengers: Endgame to defeat Thanos’ army. And while Tony Stark’s AI inside the Iron Man suit, F.R.I.D.A.Y., was present for all of this, that didn’t stop her from double-checking Dr. Strange’s math.
VisionQuest revisits a key Avengers: Endgame moment

In the second episode of VisionQuest, Vision (Paul Bettany) was badly injured by the adamantium bullets Paladin (Todd Stashwick) shot him with. J.A.R.V.I.S. (James D’Arcy) sacrificed himself to save Vision by deleting his code, reverting the power to run him back to Vision’s system, but in episode 3, it's clear Vision still needs further repairs. The remaining AIs housed in Vision’s mind scramble to help, with F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Orla Brady) taking the lead and E.D.I.T.H. (Emily Hampshire) doing what she can to assist.

F.R.I.D.A.Y. determines that she has to rewrite some of Vision’s code, and she laments that J.A.R.V.I.S. was always better at writing code than she was. “I already replaced him once,” F.R.I.D.A.Y. says, referring to J.A.R.V.I.S. Then she goes on to tell E.D.I.T.H. the important role she played for Iron Man after replacing J.A.R.V.I.S.

“I ran everything for Stark, for the Avengers. I mean, I was a younger program then,” says F.R.I.D.A.Y. “I was good. I protected heroes, saved lives, advised. I had purpose, but friends became enemies, and tyrants invaded our Earth. I was there at the end of all things. There were heroes everywhere, fighting and falling.”
Finally, she says, “I was there when Tony died. I ran over a quintillion strategic calculations that day, and I still couldn't save him. Half the world came back that day, and I lost half of mine.”
F.R.I.D.A.Y. tried a quintillion ways to save Tony Stark

This reveals some new information about Tony’s death in Avengers: Endgame. In the film, after Tony snaps his fingers, it's clear the energy from the Infinity Stones has placed him at death’s door. Rhodey (Don Cheadle) gets there first and says his goodbye, followed by Peter Parker (Tom Holland). Then Pepper Potts (Gwyneth Paltrow) arrives and says, “F.R.I.D.A.Y.?” and the AI responds, “Life functions critical,” confirming what Pepper and Tony both already knew: he was about to die.
What we didn’t know was that, throughout that day, F.R.I.D.A.Y. ran a quintillion different scenarios to try to save him, all of which came up hopeless.

When Iron Man turned to Dr. Strange in that final Endgame battle to ask, without words, “Is this the one future you spoke of?” Strange confirmed his thinking by holding up that one finger. Strange knew Tony had to sacrifice himself, and so did Tony. And if Tony knew, so did F.R.I.D.A.Y. So why did F.R.I.D.A.Y. bother running those calculations?

Of course, she was doing what she was programmed to do by monitoring Tony’s well-being while in the Iron Man suit and, if something were wrong, it was up to her to find a solution. But it also gets into a lot of the themes that VisionQuest is exploring, about the nature of these synthetic life forms and their ability to feel as well as think. F.R.I.D.A.Y. may be just a program, but she’s also a hero who aided Tony and the other Avengers many times. And, when Tony was dying, she felt the impact as much as Rhodey, Peter, and Pepper, because, like them, she was one of the closest people to Tony, even without being an actual person.

articles.headline: Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink in Ukraine — report
keyFacts: Elon Musk capped Starlink internet speeds used by Ukraine's military, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing US officials.
Restricting Starlink limits Ukraine's battlefield communications and drone operations against Russia, making some drones virtually useless, the report said.
US envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday after talks with Ukraine, a US official said.
body: Tech billionaire Elon Musk ordered the slowdown of a military-grade version of SpaceX's Starlink satellite service that Ukraine relies on, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing US officials.
Kyiv uses Starlink for battlefield communications and drone operations. Restricting the service means restricting the country's attack and defense missions against Russia.

Last week, Musk capped the speeds at which Ukrainian hardware could stay connected to the satellite-based network, the report said, citing unnamed sources. The move rendered some offensive drones and interceptor drones virtually useless, it added.
Two people told the Journal that Musk and US President Donald Trump discussed the Starlink decision in a call soon after the slowdown became public.
Some US officials, the report said, believed Musk acted unilaterally and that Trump did not specifically order retribution against Ukraine.
However, one person familiar with the situation said Musk spoke with multiple senior administration officials, including Trump, before imposing the speed cap.
Both Musk and Trump have expressed anger at Ukraine for attacking Russian diesel refineries in recent weeks, which the president blames for high energy prices.
The report also comes after Trump's comments last week that he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine losing Starlink access.
Musk had said that any limits on speed or use were decided by the US military or the president.
Musk, SpaceX, and the White House are yet to respond to the report.

US envoy Steve Witkoff is set to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday after what a US official called "constructive" talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Norway, as Trump said it was time for Ukraine to end the war.

articles.headline: Warren warns of ‘enormous risk’ to US if Musk throttled Starshield in Ukraine
keyFacts: Ukraine experienced three Starshield satellite network disruptions in the past week, failing to receive early warnings about Russian missile attacks.
Reports indicate Elon Musk restricted Ukraine's Starshield access after discussing it with President Trump, despite Musk stating the government operates it.
Senator Warren warned against Musk dictating foreign policy, while Representative Fitzpatrick called for an investigation under oath into the disruptions.
body: Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) warned of an “enormous” risk to the United States if SpaceX founder Elon Musk interfered with the speed of the Starshield communications system used by Ukraine .

Warren told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins that if Musk were responsible for the lapse in service for Ukraine’s use of the military version of his Starlink satellite network developed by SpaceX under contract with the War Department , it should be taken as a warning sign for the rest of President Donald Trump’s term.

“If it is one man, Elon Musk, who is dictating our foreign policy, then he puts the United States at enormous risk,” Warren said. “He’s the one who decides whether or not Ukraine, out there fighting on the front lines to protect its democracy, lives or dies? No, we should not have one man in that position.”
The senior senator also pointed her frustration at Trump, using the possibility that the president was behind the Starshield mishap to raise the stakes in the midterm elections .

“If Donald Trump is the one who made this decision, then I will just say that’s one more reason we need a Democratic majority in the House and the Senate, so that we can actually put some constraints on Donald Trump, so that we can investigate and get to the bottom of this,” she said. “Two more years of an unconstrained Donald Trump and two more years of an Elon Musk who does whatever he wants to do — it’s going to be an America that’s going to have a hard time surviving.”

Ukraine experienced several disruptions with its Starshield satellite network in recent history. The systems are useful tools for the war-torn country to detect and thwart Russian missiles. On three separate occasions in the past week, Ukraine didn’t receive early warnings about missile attacks.

The Wall Street Journal and CBS News each reported that Musk made the call to restrict Ukraine’s use of the satellite system despite his statement that the U.S. government owns and operates Starshield. The former outlet reported Musk and Trump discussed the decision before the restrictions.
Musk’s or Trump’s alleged involvement has led to outrage on both sides of the aisle.
Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), who has been viewed as a critic of Trump, told Collins the Starshield matter should be thoroughly investigated.

“We got to call the witnesses, got to bring them in, put them under oath, and get to the bottom of it because this is a very, very serious matter,” Fitzpatrick said. “It cannot be glossed over. We cannot just move past this. This is a serious, serious issue because lapsing Starshield in that manner costs human lives. There’s got to be consequences to that.”
Speaking specifically about the Wall Street Journal’s reporting, Fitzpatrick said if Musk were involved in such a decision, it would be illegal.
ZELENSKY SAYS HEGSETH BLOCKING MISSILES, STILL ‘NO EXPLANATION’ FOR STARSHIELD LIMITS

“When I read it, if it is in fact Mr. Musk that ordered this, that is likely a violation of the law because he has authority and decision-making authority over Starlink, the civilian commercial product, but not Starshield, which is a military-grade national security tool,” he said. “So no civilian, no individual civilian, should have any decision-making authority on how that’s deployed.”
Fitzpatrick added he would put Musk under oath as part of an investigation into what led to the disruption, saying, “You got to interview everybody.”

articles.headline: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
keyFacts: PHP maintainers announced plans to release emergency patches for two severe vulnerabilities rated 9.2 out of 10.

PHP users are advised to prepare to upgrade immediately upon release to secure their systems.
body: Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere.
PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10.
Waiting for PHP2Shell

“All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.”

The maintainers published the advisory following the leaking of purported details, which have yet to be confirmed. The report showed a video of an exploit tool dubbed PHP2Shell executing code on webservers running WordPress 7.1.3, MediaWiki 1.46.2, phpBB 3.3.17, Magento 2.4.9, Joomla 6.2.0, Laravel 13.36.0, Laravel 8.83.29, Symphony 8.1.9, Drupal 11.4.10, and WHMCS 9.0.9, all of which use PHP. A video depicting the tool has been reposted here.

Attempts to locate the unconfirmed report were unsuccessful, but security firm watchTowr said it claimed to affect every PHP version from PHP 5, released in 2004, onward. The security firm went on to say it has confirmed that the vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are real.

articles.headline: In this age of pervasive slop maybe we should be grateful for Shrek 2 Remastered
keyFacts: Shrek 2 Remastered is scheduled for release on November 10, as announced by the publisher.
Aspyr Media is handling the port, which appears to be based on the original PlayStation 2 version.
The 3D platformer features eleven levels, character switching, and support for both local and online co-op.
body: Shrek 2 Remastered is coming out in November, it has been announced. I wasn't aware there was a Shrek 2 game for PS2, the OG Xbox, GameCube and PC, probably because in 2004 I was too busy thinking about all the other games coming out. You know, stuff like Half-Life 2, World of Warcraft, Halo 2, Metal Gear Solid 3, Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas and Wings of Power: WWII Heavy Bombers and Jets.

But Shrek 2 does indeed exist, though contemporary reviews don't point to it necessarily justifying that existence. "You know folks, this game is pretty bad," wrote Nintendo World Report. "Shrek 2 is harmless, inoffensive, middle-of-the-road action for young children," Eurogamer wrote with superlative diplomacy. IGN gave it a 7 even though the reviewer "dreaded" playing it.

It's a 3D platformer, kinda, though it has some interesting features. You can switch between four characters on the go, which clearly inspired Rockstar during the making of GTA 5. It supports local and online co-op for up to four players, which is probably the best way to play it (the original only supported local). There are eleven levels, and apparently they're all quite varied, adopting various moments in the film with aplomb.

It appears to be a port of the PS2 version. The PC version of Shrek 2 was quite different to the console versions, a fact that has caused a bit of fuss in the Steam forums, though a contemporary review from Gamespot notes that "the PC version undercuts that [PS2] title with poor visuals, rougher, shallower gameplay, and an outrageously short running time."
Aspyr Media is handling the port, whose recent work includes the Lord of the Rings: War in the North re-release, and the Neverwinter Nights 2 enhanced edition.

The elephant in the news is that Shrek 2 Remastered releases on November 10, which is nine days before GTA 6. Quite how we'll all be able to wrench ourselves away from this 2004 film-to-game adaptation to suffer Rockstar's latest, I don't know.
Jokes aside: that Shrek 2 was released in 2004 does at least guarantee that humans made it.

articles.headline: 'How do you know what's real?': US utilities are making AI data centers prove they exist before handing over power connections — as 50% of planned buildouts are currently being delayed, stalled, or canceled
keyFacts: US utilities are demanding collateral, longer contracts, and study fees to weed out speculative or phantom AI data center projects.
Wood Mackenzie expects utilities to commit to only about 28% of the 1,066GW of grid connections requested by data center developers.
Exelon reported that its high-probability data center load fell from 18GW to 11GW after it began requiring transmission security agreements.
body: - US data center developers have requested 1,066GW of grid connections, but Wood Mackenzie expects utilities to commit to only about 28%
- Utilities are demanding collateral, longer contracts, and study fees; Exelon's high-probability load fell from a whopping 18GW to 11GW once it insisted on the former
- Because grid costs are shared, phantom demand risks landing on household bills, and nobody knows how much of it is real yet

US utilities and grid operators are now demanding higher rates, longer contracts, collateral, and steep engineering study fees from data center developers, in an attempt to weed out what the industry calls "phantom" data centers.

Reporting from The Wall Street Journal claims the reasoning is straightforward: Grid costs are shared, so if a utility builds substations and transmission lines for a project that never shows up, everyone else on the network ends up helping to pay for them.

The numbers back up the nerves in play: developers have requested 1,066GW of grid connections for US data centers, according to a Wood Mackenzie analysis first reported by Bloomberg in August 2026, a figure equal to roughly 83% of the country's entire utility-scale generating capacity at the end of 2025.
A queue full of ghosts as collateral becomes the norm?

Wood Mackenzie expects utilities to commit to serving only about 28% of it: roughly 12% that already has firm service commitments, plus a further 17% that looks likely. The WSJ also cites a separate Wood Mackenzie measure that puts just 23% of disclosed requests in its high-confidence category.
Much of the gap is due to duplication; developers who don't yet know which utility can deliver power fastest file the same project with several of them and keep every option open until one pans out.

Others are simply speculators: commentary in POWER Magazine argued that private equity funds, land brokers and shell companies are claiming queue positions without site control or a signed customer, betting that land with a grid connection attached will find a buyer.

The phenomenon isn't new. Utility Dive was writing about phantom data centers in 2025, and TR reported in July that 67% of electricity executives surveyed by Capgemini were seeing speculative applications for capacity. The change is that utilities are now pricing the problem, and it is causing many adverse effects.

Exelon's attempts to lock down potential consumers
Exelon, which runs utilities across the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest, offers the clearest look at what happens when developers are asked to put money down.

After it began requiring transmission security agreements (TSAs), contracts that bind customers to credit obligations, committed revenue contributions, and shortfall payments, its high-probability data center load fell nearly 40%, from 18GW at the end of 2025 to about 11GW in the second quarter. Its wider pipeline of projects under study dropped from about 43GW to 25GW.

Jeanne Jones, Exelon's CFO, told the WSJ that typical requests used to be around 50MW and now often run to 1,000MW or more. The question she kept fielding, internally and externally, was "How do you know what's real?"
Exelon, however, also told analysts its $41 billion capital plan through 2029 is unchanged, so a 40% cut in expected data center load has not, so far, shrunk the spending plan.

None of this would matter much if grid capacity were cheap, but it simply isn't. PJM, the largest US grid operator, saw its capacity auction clear at the price cap for the third time in a row this summer while missing its reliability target by 6.8GW.
In September, its independent market monitor told federal regulators that 4,017MW of forecast data center load, 42% of the growth PJM had assumed, had already been canceled or delayed.

Households are feeling the cost increase; reports in July indicated that Henrico County, Virginia, asked staff and schools to cut electricity use after a 24.9% rate increase. Virginia has also moved to stop utilities passing data center costs onto everyday users, and Texas bills are rising faster than inflation. Lindsey Short of the Ohio Manufacturers' Association warned against building the grid around "the most optimistic number on somebody's spreadsheet."

Underbuilding carries its own risks, though, especially when transformers can take years to arrive, as a recent deep dive on grid bottlenecks laid out. That is why utilities are locking in the customers they do accept. Average minimum contract lengths for large customers have risen to about 10.8 years from 4.6 before 2024, according to filings aggregated by Halcyon and cited by the Journal, and a separate research brief built on Halcyon's tracker found a similar jump.

What nobody can yet say is how much of the AI power rush is real, and that poses problems for planners, stakeholders, and households alike. Until it does, utilities are doing what any lender would: asking to see the money first; households just happen to be roadkill if things don't pan out.

articles.headline: Marvel's VisionQuest Episodes 3 and 4 Review: 'Reboot' and 'Malware'
keyFacts: Episodes 3 and 4 of Marvel's VisionQuest are currently streaming on Disney+ and feature Paul Bettany's synthetic hero working to understand his emotions.
The reviewer stated that James Spader's Ultron betrays his family at the end of Episode 4, setting up an exciting conflict for Episode 5.
The reviewer noted that the series successfully stands on its own without requiring viewers to watch Agatha All Along.
body: Full spoilers follow for VisionQuest Episodes 3 and 4, which are streaming now on Disney+.

VisionQuest is turning out to be quite the pleasant little surprise. What initially seemed like an obligatory but unneeded follow-up to a loose end from WandaVision is rapidly developing into a series with plenty of heart, soul, and depth of its own. It never pays to count out Paul Bettany's synthetic hero.

Mind you, entertaining as the first two episodes were, my one real reservation with VisionQuest out of the gate was that it was a bit difficult to connect with this version of Bettany's character. As he himself says, he has all the memories of the original Vision but none of his soul. Given how poignant and utterly human Vision was in his past MCU appearances, seeing a cold, aloof, emotionless copy of that character takes some getting used to.

But that problem quickly starts to fade in Episodes 3 and 4. Already, White Vision is making great strides in terms of understanding his emotions and internal conflict and embracing this side of himself he doesn't quite understand. Compared to the Loki series , which basically relied on a quick-and-dirty speedrun to transform the 2012-era Loki (Tom Hiddleston) into something more resembling his post- Thor: Ragnarok self, this feels like a more coherent and purposeful way of bridging the gap between two wildly different versions of an MCU character.

Certainly, Bettany has a lot more to work with in these two episodes, both comedically and dramatically. His malfunctioning processors give the actor some welcome opportunity to deploy a bit of physical comedy in Episode 3. And both episodes make the most of the rapidly deepening bond between Vision and Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica). By all rights, their relationship should feel rushed, but somehow it all works anyway. By the time Vision is coaxing his son on how to reboot him in the hotel swimming pool, he feels well on the road to reclaiming that lost humanity that was so vital to the original character. That process continues in Episode 4, where Vision pointedly stops drawing such a hard distinction between his past and present selves.

I also appreciate how well the show's writers are succeeding in not making Agatha All Along required viewing. This isn't a show you want to watch without at least having seen WandaVision, but it also does a fine job of explaining everything you need to know about Tommy's bizarre existence without making his brother Billy's (Joe Locke) parallel journey into mandatory homework. It helps the series stand on its own two feet a bit more, rather than simply being the final act of a trilogy.

Another big plus in VisionQuest's favor is that it features such a lovable supporting cast of AI goofballs. James Spader's Ultron doesn't steal the show to quite the degree he did in the first two episodes, but he remains one of the absolute highlights of the series. Ultron is great for both periodic comedic relief and the sorts of knowing observations on human nature that used to be Vision's purview. But we also get to see the character finally take a more purposeful step onto center stage late in Episode 4, as he manipulates his way into taking the wheel (literally) and predictably betrays his family at his first opportunity. The prospect of an Ultron fully in control and back in the physical world is a very exciting one heading into Episode 5.

Speaking of Vision's family, we get a lot of great scenes involving F.R.I.D.A.Y. (Orla Brady), E.D.I.T.H. (Emily Hampshire), and even D.U.M.-E. (Henry Lewis) and U (Jonathan Sayer). The series is doing a fantastic job of fleshing out and enriching these characters that used to be nothing more than disembodied voices or slapstick workshop tools. Episode 4 is particularly strong when it comes to exploring their own emotional journeys and how much they parallel what Vision is experiencing.
Read Last Week's VisionQuest Review
VisionQuest Episodes 1 & 2 Review

None of this is to say the series isn't still experiencing some growing pains. Episodes 3 and 4 feel a bit clunky in how they handle the transition from a conflict mostly built around Paladin (Todd Stashwick) to one centered around Jocasta (T'Nia Miller). The former character basically drops out of the picture after running afoul of the latter. Still, I'm enjoying the show's take on Jocasta so far. She's nothing if not sympathetic so far, and she holds a lot of potential as both a villain and the object of Ultron's fascination. All in all, these two episodes do a lot to set up a compelling conflict for the second half of the series.

articles.headline: How much power can a 1kW wind turbine produce for your home?
keyFacts: A one-kilowatt home wind turbine can produce about two thousand four hundred kilowatt-hours of energy per year under optimal conditions, according to the article.
The Department of Energy recommends placing a turbine rotor at least thirty feet above obstacles, which often conflicts with local zoning height rules.
Installing a residential wind turbine typically costs between twenty thousand and fifty thousand dollars, significantly more than comparable solar panel installations.
body: How much power can a 1kW wind turbine produce for your home?
It all depends on the wind.

Do home wind turbines actually work? The answer is a very reserved "yes." With solar energy cruising into record territory, small-scale wind power for residential use tends to get lost in the sun (poor pun intended).There are several caveats, though wind power is not an altogether losing proposition. It really depends on the need and the scale of use. They even make compact turbines for powering RVs, so it also depends on your definition of "home."

It's important to note that a 1 kW turbine is a "peak" power measure, not necessarily what you'll get out of it. The more useful number to look at is annual or monthly energy production, measured in kilowatt-hours. In a carefully chosen position, a 1 kW turbine could feasibly produce 200 kWh per month, or about 2,400 kWh per year. That works out to under a quarter of the average US household's annual energy consumption.

None of this is to say that wind turbines are weak power producers — it just depends on the wind. If you live in an area with annual wind speeds averaging 14+ mph, this is something worth looking into. If not, or if windy days are sparse or even average, maybe not so much. A 1 kW system is feasible, but it's best to look at it in terms of supplemental power for an already efficient home.
Placement determines whether it works

A wind turbine for a home practically requires a high average wind speed that's consistent month-to-month. Homes with lots of trees, surrounded by other homes, behind hills or with large sheds need not apply. Not only do these obstacles block wind, but they also create turbulence, which reduces output and speeds up wear and tear on the turbine. The Department of Energy's small wind guidance recommends placing the bottom of the rotor at least 30 feet above any obstacle within 300 horizontal feet of the tower.

That recommendation alone tells you all you need to know about placing a wind turbine in a suburban neighborhood. It'll make for some interesting conversations at the neighbor's house, and little more. Worse, most local zoning rules limit structures to around 35 feet, and wind turbines often require much more in order to clear nearby trees and rooftops. A rooftop installation option sounds great on paper, but it can transmit vibration and noise directly into your rooftop, a lovely side effect while trying to catch some Zs before work.

If you're sold on wind power, look beyond your region's wind map, check local zoning and utility rules and conduct a thorough assessment of your site's obstacles and average wind direction. It's also a good idea to get an installer to estimate overall production before spending your hard-earned dough.
A whole-house turbine needs much more capacity

If your home is a small, economical little cabin or a permanently parked RV, a 1kW wind turbine is certainly an option. However, it's not enough to power a typical US home. The average household uses about 10,500 kWh of electricity per year (around 850 kWh per month), and a residential turbine in the 5 kW to 15 kW range is necessary to put a dent in that power consumption.

Cost is another reason to proceed with a bit of caution. It'll run the average consumer between $20,000 and $50,000 to toss up a wind turbine. Installing solar panels with the same energy production in mind is roughly $2,500 to $3,500, and that's before incentives are calculated in.

A grid-connected system typically requires an inverter as well and can offset some utility use when the wind is blowing. Off-grid systems will require batteries and a charge controller to store power. For the majority of suburban dwellers, improving insulation and tossing in some ground- or roof-mounted solar panels will provide more dependable, solid results. If you want to go the wind route, it makes the most sense in open, rural areas that have verified average wind speeds and a place to put your tower.
